sourceFingerprintAlgorithm: sha256 over the covered paths in DECLARED ORDER; each path contributes <repo-relative path> NUL <64-hex sha256 of the file's RAW BYTES> NUL; per-file digest = script/m24/portability.ts sha256File() (node:crypto, no process spawn)
failures: A1: every served position EQUALS the index-stored line for its own row (differential against the store, not a recomputation)
A1: the measurement is not vacuous — the real index served EXACT call sites, differentially checked against their own stored rows

A1-SOURCE: the served line's own text usually NAMES the callee — a rate near zero would mean the store's lines are unrelated to their rows and the differential above would be arithmetically right and semantically empty

index.selectionRule: most relationship rows (326968), ties broken by path
index.selectionCaveat: machine-local: these numbers describe ONE index on ONE machine. Reproducing them elsewhere needs `--db` pointed at an equivalent index. The rule is declared and deterministic (most relationship rows, ties by path) so two runs on an unchanged store read the same input — the first version of this harness picked the NEWEST index by mtime and two consecutive runs read different stores (601 checked positions vs 7), which is the §8.2 failure one level up: a byte-stable record carrying an unstable claim.

rowAccountability.harnessDefectFoundAndFixed: The first version of A2-STORE ignored the §11.7 launch gate and reported 73 'unaccounted rows' on the 765k-row index — every one a yaml/python file the launch set had refused on purpose. Reading a declared absence as a missing row is precisely what §11.7 calls a violation, and the harness was committing it against the component. The gate is now counted as declared absence.

plantedDefects.detail: served line points at the caller's DECLARATION while the payload keeps the store's line (only a source-text check sees this): caught by A2-STORE | a served position is attributed to a rowId the store does not hold: caught by A2-STORE | an omission counter is zeroed, so a row vanishes with nothing declared: BLOCKED — among the rows this surface actually serves on this index, 0 are unpositionable (the index holds 0 NULL-line rows, all behind the launch gate or the relation vocabulary), so zeroing an already-zero counter is a no-op and the gate was never engaged. Judged on the fixture instead (verify-navigation.ts U4/U5 and their mutants).
plantedDefects.blockedNote: A plant whose precondition the real index does not meet is BLOCKED with its reason and excluded from the denominator, rather than counted as a survivor. The omission-counter law is exercised on the fixture instead (verify-navigation.ts U4/U5 and their mutants).
plantedDefects.discriminationNote: The served-line name test (A1-SOURCE) does NOT, on this index, discriminate a declaration position from a call-site position: the caller's declaration line of a multi-line function often contains the callee's name further down, so the text test passes. The accounting law (A2-STORE) is what catches that plant here. The name test's discriminating power is proven on the FIXTURE instead, where the caller's declaration is a single line with no call sites on it (verify-navigation.ts, mutant 'the old declaration position is served for a stored call site').

§15.1.claim: textDocument/references and the graph/usages surface run the SAME relation vocabulary (src/lsp/relations.ts isUsageSiteRow) over the SAME stored rows, so they agree on WHICH rows are usages. They differ in ONE declared respect: references emits ONE LOCATION PER STORED ROW (`path:line:rowId`), while a surface that groups per symbol renders ONE GROUP per symbol (§13.1). The payload carries `totalCount` (rows), the omission counters, and `callSite.rowId` on every location, so the multiplicity is visible rather than reconciled away.
§15.1.filter: isUsageSiteRow — declaration containments (contains/exports) and self-references are excluded by both surfaces; that exclusion is the declared filter, and it is the shared owner's predicate rather than either surface's copy.

limitations: One real index, read-only, at the mtime named above. Per-language call-site coverage is M59's lane (A7); the counts here describe THIS index, not the corpus.

A symbol whose stored call-site line is a real integer is served a LINE-ONLY range, because brain_relationship stores no column for a call site. An editor places the caret at the start of that line; the exact token needs M59's column.

The declaration substitute is served with the calling symbol's byte-accurate range, so a client that renders a substitute must label it — the payload's callSite.note is the label, and src/lsp/server.ts does not currently forward callSite to the wire (see the L3 record's wiringNeededInServerTs).
Position equality is asserted against the stored row and against the file's own line count. It is not asserted against a rendered editor frame; that is a §15.5 screenshot leg, not this one.

determinism.note: Every number here is read from the index named above and is therefore stable for that index. Two runs against the SAME unmodified index reproduce the record byte-for-byte modulo the three declared fields. Re-indexing the project changes the input and the numbers with it — the index path and mtime are recorded so a reader can tell which.
